transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 0:42:00
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carlos (Equinox CTO), Maya (ML Eng), Samir (Product)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on model selection and deployment mode. Key requirements: ~20-30k token context for long documents, multilingual support (EN/ES/JA), tool-calling/function calling for structured data lookup, preference for hosted to start but private/VPC for PII later. Request for benchmarks and security docs.

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro, I'm Alex from Redwood, this is Priya our SE, and we wanted to understand where you are in eval and what your biggest constraints are.
00:14 Carlos: Hey Alex, thanks. I'm Carlos, CTO at Equinox. We run a docs ingestion pipeline for legal and engineering docs; primary ask is summarization and question answering across long contracts, also multilingual support.
00:28 Priya: Got it, and when you say long contracts, are we talking pages or long single-file contexts? like 8k, 16k, 32k?
00:36 Maya: We're seeing anywhere 15k to 25k tokens per doc once we concat related appendices. Ideally 32k would be great.
00:47 Alex: That's helpful — Redwood supports hosted and dedicated and private. For initial pilots hosted is fastest; dedicated gives predictable throughput if you want reserved GPU pools; private/VPC for later when PHI/PII and compliance are gating.
01:01 Samir: Budget's a factor — we need to balance latency and cost, so curious how model selection impacts that. Also we use Spanish and Japanese occasionally, and need tool calling to fetch structured metadata from our internal index.
01:17 Priya: For multilingual we usually recommend models with strong multi-lingual pretraining — Mistral variants and Falcon have good footprints, Llama 3/2 variants also okay depending on license and hallucination profile. For 32k context, there are a few open models and quantized builds that can handle it, but throughput and cost change a lot.
01:35 Carlos: When you say Mistral variants, is that mixtral? I always mix up the names, and how does that compare to Falcon for longer context?
01:44 Priya: Yeah Mixtral 8x is the new Mistral long-context friendly model, it's often better at instruction-following vs raw Falcon, Falcon tends to be faster at lower precision on specific infra. There's also Llama-based 30k-context forks but licensing and quantization matter. Our team usually benchmarks a candidate set: Mistral mixtral, Falcon-40B-32k, and a Llama 3 or Llama 2 70B- 32k variant if licensing allows.
02:10 Carlos: We prefer open models to avoid API lock-in. Also curious about function calling — can Redwood hosted call out to our tool endpoints or do we need Private/VPC for that?
02:22 Alex: Hosted supports function/tool calling via the API — you can define functions and Redwood will stream responses and structured tool call outputs. For sensitive data you can route tool calls through a VPC/private deployment or use dedicated with private networking. Hosted keeps logs in our control plane unless you enable onboarded retention controls; for strict compliance we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS.
02:40 Maya: Any gotchas with streaming and KV cache when using long context? We wanted low latency for interactive QA UI but also to batch for cost.
02:49 Priya: Streaming is orthogonal to batching and KV cache — for interactive use you can enable streaming; KV cache helps with repeated prefixes. For long context workloads KV cache savings are smaller if requests are mostly unique, but batching and automatic prefix caching can reduce per-token cost if you have repeat patterns.
03:10 Samir: Do we need to rewrite the infra to hit dedicated? Our infra is in GCP with private routes and we use internal KMS.
03:18 Alex: Dedicated can be provisioned in specific cloud regions and we support private-network peering. For full customer-managed KMS and audit logs you can opt for Private. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and lower variable cost on throughput.
03:31 Carlos: Security wise we need SOC 2, ISO, audit logs, SSO. Can you email the security pack?
03:36 Alex: Absolutely, I'll send SOC 2 report, ISO summary, SOC docs and our VPC playbook.
03:41 Priya: On the model side, for your workloads I'd suggest we benchmark: mixtral-8x, falcon-40b-32k (quantized Q4), and a Llama 2 70B-32k if licensing is fine. We'll run latency, token cost, and hallucination/regression tests against your prompt set.
04:00 Maya: That would be great. Also our app needs tool-calling that returns JSON with specific schema; how do we validate structured outputs?
04:10 Priya: Redwood supports function calling and structured outputs — we can return JSON and schema validation hooks. There are some minor variations in model outputs; part of the benchmark is to run schema validation and measure mismatch rates.
04:27 Carlos: Any comments on quantization — we heard 4-bit helps cost but affects accuracy.
04:33 Priya: Correct — 4-bit (Q4) quantization reduces memory and cost but can slightly change logits. For many tasks it's fine; for high-precision QA you might prefer 8-bit or fp16. We'll include both q4 and fp16 baselines in the bench.
04:50 Samir: Timeline — we want a POC in 4 weeks. Is that realistic?
04:55 Alex: Yes, a 4-week pilot is common: week 1 onboarding + sample data and security review, week 2 bench runs, week 3 integrate tool-calls & UI, week 4 validate and iterate.
05:06 Maya: For data residency, some docs are EU-only, will hosted store data in US? We need EU residency for some sets.
05:15 Alex: We have regional hosting and can route EU traffic to EU regions. For strict residency and audit control, Private is simplest. We'll include residency options in the doc bundle.
05:27 Priya: Quick question on failover — if you run dedicated and it saturates, Redwood can fallback to hosted variants with routing policies to preserve uptime. That may change response shape slightly, we can configure automatic fallback policies.
05:44 Carlos: Nice. What about cost ballpark — mixtral vs falcon?
05:49 Priya: It varies by throughput and quantization. Roughly, a quantized Falcon-32k on dedicated GPUs might be cheaper per token than an fp16 Mixtral for same latency; we'll surface real numbers from bench.
06:02 Samir: Do you have customers with similar long-context multilingual setups?
06:07 Alex: Yes, a couple of legal-tech and medtech customers run 16-32k contexts, multilingual. We can anonymize references.
06:14 Carlos: For the benchmark, can we simulate our QA UI load pattern — many short interactive queries plus occasional long summarization jobs?
06:23 Priya: Absolutely — provide sample traffic distribution and we'll run throughput and p95 latency measurements.
06:31 Maya: Is streaming supported for the long summarization jobs or is it better to return full payloads?
06:36 Priya: For user-facing interactive summaries streaming gives better perceived latency; for batch jobs full payloads are fine. Both supported.
06:44 Carlos: Any limitations with tool calling in hosted environment — like outbound firewall rules?
06:49 Alex: Hosted can make outbound calls to public endpoints. For internal-only endpoints you'd want VPC or a proxy. We can discuss connector patterns in the deep dive.
06:58 Maya: What about rate limits in hosted during the pilot? We don't expect huge TPS but bursts could happen.
07:04 Alex: We'll set quotas and can open bursts for pilots. Dedicated removes most shared rate limits since you get reserved capacity.
07:12 Samir: On licensing, we need to confirm open model licenses; if we want to fine-tune or use Llama we need to check terms.
07:20 Priya: We'll include model licensing notes in the bench deck — e.g., Llama variants have Meta license caveats for commercial products; Mistral and Falcon are generally permissive but check the exact versions.
07:32 Carlos: Great. OK let's recap next steps.
07:36 Alex: Recap: I'll send pricing + security pack; Priya will run the bench (mixtral, falcon q4, llama 32k) against your sample prompts; Maya will send sample prompts and traffic profile; schedule a technical deep dive for VPC/KMS next week.
07:50 Maya: I'll upload the sample set by tomorrow.
07:53 Carlos: Sounds good. If benchmarks look good we'll likely start with hosted pilot then move to dedicated or private in Q2 depending on compliance.
08:02 Alex: Perfect — thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email and update CRM with the action items.

Notes: occasional transcript artifacts and overlaps in speaker IDs; some model names transcribed loosely (mixtral vs mixtrail). References: sample benchmark spreadsheet link (shared), security pack link (will be shared).
